paired.comparison: Actual Source EventLogReporter with SDK processor and HTTP collector versus actual Native EventLogReporter over a controlled exporter port. Compare complete batch documents/bytes, overflow and zero-queue behavior, batch-size clamping, timer, processor timeout progression, failure warnings and emission after shutdown.

verification.native: 12 passed: ordinary-event batching corpus, independent shutdown signal subscriptions/waiter cancellation, emitted attribute ownership and observation time, plus direct Session channel/record/wire regressions.
verification.source: 39 actual ordinary-event SDK channel/HTTP cases; unchanged pinned OTel package 34 tests already passed C8-GE.
verification.scope_reason: Covers the new count channel and its providers, with timeout overlap and shutdown ownership cases that differ from the Session channel.

behavior: Queue overflow silently discards records; an oversized configured batch count is clamped to queue capacity. Full batches start immediately and partial batches use the configured timer.
Processor timeout permits subsequent batches while the transport remains owned by the exporter. Timeout itself does not invoke the business onFailure callback; a later failed export still does.
Emission captures observation time and caller attributes. Queued ordinary events use the already qualified default SDK attribute admission and OTLP serialization.

Shutdown closes admission, snapshots accepted records for sequential flushing, drains the exporter and releases per-call cancellation subscriptions. Cancelling a Python waiter leaves the shared cleanup running; each shutdown caller can still provide its own abort signal.
limitations: Paired channel observations use a controlled Native exporter port; end-to-end service/production consumer composition remains follow-up work.

SDK diagnostics, self-observability metrics and pathological invalid processor values outside typed consumer options are not fully reproduced. No implicit span-context or exception enrichment parity claim is established here.
Full migration/release, Portable/browser and Windows 7 qualification remain pending.
